newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-BENT WINS MEN'S 100 BACKSTROKE WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-BENT WINS MEN'S 100 BACKSTROKE WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Cuba's Neisser Bent swept his second backstroke title at the world short-course swimming championships when he won the 100 event on Sunday.
Bent, winner of Friday's 200 backstroke, trailed American Brian Retterer at the halfway mark of the 100 but came through smoothly on the last length to win in a championship record 52.77.
Retterer took the silver in 53.06 and Australia's Adrian Radley the bronze in 53.36.
Bent's fellow Cuban Rodolfo Falcon, who won both backstroke events at the 1995 world short-course championships in Rio de Janeiro, finished out of the medals in fourth place (53.48).
